name: Medici Blue
lede: Medici Blue is a greyed, muted blue-green from Robert Ridgway's 1912 color standards, and no book we hold confirms whether the name points to the Florentine family or to someone else entirely.

sections.title: A name the books leave open
sections.body:
Ridgway placed this color on plate XLVIII of his 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature*, and Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates it to 1905 on their plate 37 [1]. A darker variant, [[deep-medici-blue|Deep Medici Blue]], sits two plates away and is listed as a near-duplicate of the ISCC-NBS block "Greyish Blue-Green" [1][2]. Whether the name honors the Medici banking family, famous for patronizing Florentine art and fashion, or some other namesake, is undocumented in the sources we hold [1][3].

The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 also files it close to its own "Greyish Blue-Green" and "Deep Bluish Grey-Green" blocks, suggesting it was treated as one of a small family of muted blue-greens rather than a singular shade [2].

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body: Measured in LCH terms it is lightness 58, chroma 10, hue 195 degrees: a pale, low-saturation blue-green closer to grey than to any pure blue [3]. Its nearest library neighbor is [[titmouse-blue|Titmouse Blue]], about 3.2 units away, with the paler [[celestial-blue|Celestial Blue]] close behind [3]. Next to [[slate]] or [[petrol]] it reads as the greyer, quieter one [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this blue-green, as photographed, in 303 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.3 percent [4]. Its heaviest use is in watercolor sketches and marine scenes: a John Singer Sargent Alpine study from 1870, P. S. Krøyer's 1899 beach painting *Boys Bathing at Skagen*, and Monet's 1904 *Waterloo Bridge, London, at Dusk* [4]. These are computed color matches on aged, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [4].

questions.q: True or false: the books consulted confirm Medici Blue is named for the Florentine Medici family.
Which color is listed as a near-duplicate of Medici Blue in the ISCC-NBS system?

openers: Medici Blue has carried its name since at least 1905, and no book we hold says for certain who or what it honors.

issues: Naming origin undocumented in the books consulted.
